# `silk/schema/json_schema`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Describe a `Schema` type as a JSON Schema, for validators, editors, and AI tools.

## When to use
Call [`JsonSchemas.write`](#JsonSchemas.impl.write) with the `silk.schema.shape.Shapes` of a type, from
`silk.schema.schema.Schemas.shape`, to write its JSON Schema to the ambient `Writer`. Pick a
[`JsonSchemaDialect`](#JsonSchemaDialect) for where the schema goes: `Standard` for validators and MCP tools, and
the strict dialects for a model's structured output or tool parameters. Call
[`JsonSchemas.writeVariant`](#JsonSchemas.impl.writeVariant) for the parameters of one tool, when a union lists the tools.

## Details
The output is JSON Schema draft 2020-12. Structs are objects with their fields' wire names, unit
unions are an `enum` of names, and unions with fields are a `oneOf` of one object per variant,
whose tag property holds the variant's name. A named type that the root uses is an entry in
`$defs`, used through `$ref`, so recursive types work; the root itself is written in place. Doc
comments become `description`. `Spec` rules become `minimum`, `maxLength`, `pattern` and the
like, and a field's default becomes `default`.

A rule the dialect has no keyword for, a codec's check, or a rule about a value after a codec
changed it, goes into `description` as text instead, and the schema is then approximate: it
accepts at least what the decoder accepts, never less. [`JsonSchemas.write`](#JsonSchemas.impl.write) returns whether it
is exact, and an approximate schema uses `anyOf` where an exact one uses `oneOf`.

The dialects follow the providers' documented subsets:

- `Standard`: all of the above, with `$schema`. MCP tool schemas use it.
- `OpenAiStrict`: the root is an object, every property is required and a field that may be
  absent is nullable instead, every object has `additionalProperties: false`, and `const`,
  `oneOf`, `minLength`, `maxLength` and `default` are not used.
- `AnthropicStrict`: every object has `additionalProperties: false`, and there are no numeric,
  length or count keywords and no `default`. A recursive type is an error.
- `Gemini`: no `const`, `oneOf`, `pattern`, length keywords or `default`.

## Examples
### Write the JSON Schema of a config
```silk
import silk.core.effect { Effect }
import silk.io.writer { Writer, WriterError }
import silk.mem.allocator { Allocator, OutOfMemoryError }
import silk.schema.json_schema { JsonSchemaDialect, JsonSchemaError, JsonSchemaOptions, JsonSchemas }
import silk.schema.schema { Schema, Schemas, Spec }

/// A server to start.
struct Server {
  /// The port to listen on.
  pub port: u16,
}

impl Schema for Server {
  static fn spec() -> Spec<Server> {
    return Spec<Server>.of() |> Spec<Server>.between("port", 1, 65535)
  }
}

struct Capture {
  length: usize,
}

impl Writer for Capture {
  effect fn writeAll(self: &mut Self, val: &[u8]) -> () ! WriterError ? &mut Writer {
    self.length = self.length + val.length
    return ()
  }
  effect fn flush(self: &mut Self) -> () ! WriterError ? &mut Writer { return () }
}

effect fn check() -> bool ! JsonSchemaError | WriterError | OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Allocator {
  let shapes = run Schemas.shape<Server>()
  let mut capture = Capture {length: 0}
  // {"$schema":"https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema","type":"object","properties":
  //  {"port":{"type":"integer","minimum":1,"maximum":65535,"description":"The port to listen on."}},
  //  "required":["port"],"description":"A server to start."}
  let exact = run JsonSchemas.write(&shapes, JsonSchemaOptions.of(JsonSchemaDialect.Standard))
    |> Effect.provideMut<Writer>(&mut capture)
  return exact && capture.length > 0
}

pub effect fn main() -> i32 ! JsonSchemaError | WriterError | OutOfMemoryError {
  let mut allocator = Allocator.systemAllocatorProvider()
  let exact = run check() |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
  return if exact { 0 } else { 1 }
}
```

Import as `JsonSchemas` with `import silk.schema.json_schema { JsonSchemas }`.

<a id="JsonSchemas.impl.write"></a>

### Associated function `write`

```silk
pub effect fn write(shapes: &Shapes, options: JsonSchemaOptions) -> bool
    ! JsonSchemaError | WriterError | OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Writer | &mut Allocator
```

Writes the JSON Schema of the root of `shapes` to the ambient `Writer`, as compact JSON, and
returns whether it is exact: whether every rule became a keyword.

#### Errors

- `JsonSchemaError` if the dialect cannot describe the type.
- `WriterError` if the `Writer` fails.
- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the bookkeeping.

<a id="JsonSchemas.impl.writeVariant"></a>

### Associated function `writeVariant`

```silk
pub effect fn writeVariant(shapes: &Shapes, variant: &VariantShape, options: JsonSchemaOptions) -> bool
    ! JsonSchemaError | WriterError | OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Writer | &mut Allocator
```

Writes the JSON Schema of the object of `variant`'s fields, without its tag, as the
parameters of a tool. `shapes` holds the shapes `variant` refers to. Returns whether it is
exact.

#### Errors

- `JsonSchemaError` if the dialect cannot describe a field's type.
- `WriterError` if the `Writer` fails.
- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the bookkeeping.
